findings.observed: In both mocked boundaries, control(user) changes owner/generation before dispatch, then waits for run.lock. The current operation subsequently dispatches a mocked click while transfer is pending. No click is demonstrated after control() has completed.
findings.interpretation: The current lock entry is deliberately the atomic action boundary. RunPause also explicitly allows already-running tools to settle. This is not evidence that human ownership after completed transfer can be bypassed.
findings.minimal_suggestion: If takeover should suppress browser input that has not yet been dispatched, carry the captured generation into the dispatcher and check owner/transferring/generation at the first input boundary after target/nested resolution. Reject with execution=not_executed; let already-dispatched effects settle. A single pre-await check before asyncio.wait_for is weaker because task scheduling introduces a yield. Target preparation currently scrolls/focuses too; avoid promising that no page-side input can occur unless that preparation is also guarded.
findings.acceptance: Pause during the actual target/nested CDP await, request takeover, release the await; pending mutation dispatch count remains 0 and returned receipt is not_executed. Separate case requests takeover after dispatch: exactly one input settles and no retry occurs.

findings.observed: timeout_ms accepts 0..10000; wait maps 0 to 10000. Its deadline is checked only after awaited evaluate, and it does not include post-condition observation/page_state. A requested 1 ms takes about 81 ms with one mocked 80 ms CDP evaluation, or with immediate satisfaction and mocked 80 ms post-observation. The 35 s wait_for starts only around _action; target gets a separate 5 s bound and nested DOM resolution occurs outside the 35 s watchdog.
findings.interpretation: Condition deadline and transport/action watchdog are different budgets; increasing timeout_ms is not the main reliability fix. The nested-resolution path has no explicit enclosing service deadline; a lower CDP layer may still apply one, so do not claim unbounded systemwide waiting.
findings.minimal_suggestion: Use an explicit budget for target plus nested resolution, and pass remaining condition time to each CDP wait. Give post-observation a small separate budget and retain dispatch progress in the receipt. Document condition timeout separately from whole-operation watchdog.
findings.acceptance: A slow mocked CDP call cannot arbitrarily extend the condition budget; nested resolution resolves/rejects within a finite explicit budget; completed submission followed by observer timeout is never automatically replayed.

challenge_stable_ax_ref.conclusion: Do not copy all refs into allegedly stable Codex AX indices.
challenge_stable_ax_ref.evidence: Codex report: AX revision/diff exists, but WASM index allocation was not decompiled; semantic snapshots and AX input have different namespaces. No general proof of indices stable across navigation, takeover or DOM replacement. Project already binds refs to the latest observation and document/generation.
challenge_stable_ax_ref.adopt_instead: Keep current invalidation contract. Add scoped observations / pagination and structured model-context projection first. If incremental observations are added, explicitly bind each delta to a base observation and document; retain IDs only for nodes whose identity is verified. Add semantic role/name + container/frame scope for resilience, separate from opaque ref identity.
challenge_stable_ax_ref.scope: These are design recommendations from shipped/local evidence, not a reverse-engineered stable AX allocation algorithm.
